question: Theoretical foundations of Bharatanatyam have been found in which of these Shastras?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Natya Shastra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The theoretical foundations of Bharatanatyam (and of Indian classical dance and drama in general) are found in the Natya Shastra, an ancient Sanskrit treatise on the performing arts attributed to Sage Bharata Muni. (नाट्य शास्त्र — भरतनाट्यम)

 

• The Natya Shastra is believed to have been composed between 200 BCE and 200 CE and deals with dramaturgy, dance, music, aesthetics (rasa theory) and stagecraft.

 

• Bharatanatyam, one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu and is traditionally traced back to the principles laid down in the Natya Shastra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Natya Shastra propounds the Rasa theory, describing nine principal rasas (navarasa) — the aesthetic emotions evoked through performance.

 

• Other classical dance forms of India include Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi and Sattriya.

 

NOTE

 

• Arth Shastra (Option 1): Written by Kautilya (Chanakya), it is a treatise on statecraft, economics and military strategy, unrelated to dance.

 

• Vaimānika Shāstra (Option 2): An early 20th-century text purportedly on ancient aeronautics, unrelated to the performing arts.

 

• Dharma Shastra (Option 3): A body of ancient legal and religious texts dealing with duty, law and conduct, not dance theory.

question: Which tunnel has been built with ultra-modern specifications in the Pir Panjal range of the Himalayas at an altitude of 3000 metres above Mean Sea Level?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atal Tunnel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Atal Tunnel is a highway tunnel built under the Rohtang Pass in the Pir Panjal range of the Himalayas, at an altitude of about 3,000 metres (10,000 feet) above Mean Sea Level. (अटल सुरंग — पीर पंजाल श्रेणी)

 

• It connects Manali in Himachal Pradesh to the Lahaul-Spiti valley, providing all-weather connectivity that was earlier cut off for nearly six months a year due to snow.

 

• At about 9.02 km, it was, at the time of its inauguration in October 2020 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the longest highway tunnel above 10,000 feet in the world. It is built with ultra-modern specifications, including a semi-transverse ventilation system and emergency egress tunnels.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tunnel was originally named the Rohtang Tunnel and was later renamed the Atal Tunnel after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

 

• It reduces the road distance between Manali and Leh by about 46 km and travel time by four to five hours.

 

NOTE

 

• Jawahar Tunnel (Option 1): Located on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway through the Pir Panjal range, but it is an older tunnel, not the one described here.

 

• Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel (Option 2): A tunnel on the Jammu-Srinagar highway (Chenani-Nashri Tunnel), India's longest road tunnel at lower altitude, not at 3,000 m.

 

• Bhatan Tunnel (Option 3): Not a well-known Himalayan tunnel matching this description; included as a distractor.

question: In which Five-Year Plan was the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana started?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seventh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY) was launched on 28 April 1989 during the Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990) by merging the National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) and the Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP). (जवाहर रोजगार योजना — सातवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• Its main objective was to generate additional gainful employment for the unemployed and underemployed in rural areas through the creation of durable community assets.

 

• It was implemented mainly through village panchayats, marking an important step in decentralised rural employment planning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Jawahar Rozgar Yojana was later restructured and renamed the Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana (JGSY) in 1999.

 

• The Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990) focused on the objectives of rapid foodgrain production, increased employment generation and productivity.

 

NOTE

 

• Fourth Plan (Option 2, 1969-74): Known for the Green Revolution and the policy of "Growth with Stability"; did not launch JRY.

 

• Sixth Plan (Option 3, 1980-85): Introduced schemes like NREP and IRDP, which were later merged into JRY, but JRY itself began in the Seventh Plan.

 

• Fifth Plan (Option 4, 1974-78): Focused on removal of poverty (Garibi Hatao) and self-reliance; JRY was not launched in this plan.

question: Identify the element that does NOT belong to Period 6 of Modern Periodic Table.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Silicon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Silicon (Si, atomic number 14) belongs to Period 3, Group 14 of the Modern Periodic Table, not Period 6. (सिलिकॉन — आवर्त 3)

 

• Period 6 of the periodic table spans elements from Caesium (Cs, 55) to Radon (Rn, 86), and includes the lanthanide series (57-71) placed separately at the bottom.

 

• Tungsten (W, 74), Rhenium (Re, 75) and Platinum (Pt, 78) are all transition metals located in Period 6, in the d-block.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Silicon is a metalloid, widely used in the semiconductor and electronics industry, and is the second most abundant element in the Earth's crust after oxygen.

 

• Other well-known Period 6 elements include Barium, Gold (Au), Mercury (Hg) and Lead (Pb).

 

NOTE

 

• Tungsten (Option 2): A Period 6, Group 6 transition metal, known for having the highest melting point of any metal.

 

• Rhenium (Option 3): A Period 6, Group 7 transition metal, one of the rarest elements in the Earth's crust.

 

• Platinum (Option 4): A Period 6, Group 10 transition metal, a dense, precious metal used in jewellery and catalytic converters.

question: The Prime Minister in August 2021 announced the fortification of rice distributed under various government schemes including the Public Distribution System (PDS) and Mid-Day-Meal scheme by the year _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2024.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 15 August 2021, during his Independence Day address, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that rice distributed under all government schemes — including the Public Distribution System (PDS), Mid-Day Meal Scheme and ICDS — would be fortified by 2024. (चावल फोर्टिफिकेशन — 2024 तक)

 

• The scheme, called the National Food Security Act (NFSA) Rice Fortification, is implemented by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution to address widespread micronutrient deficiencies (anaemia) among the population.

 

• Fortified rice is enriched with iron, folic acid and Vitamin B-12, produced by blending Fortified Rice Kernels (FRK) with normal rice in a 1:100 ratio.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The rollout was implemented in a phased manner: covering the ICDS and PM POSHAN (Mid-Day Meal) schemes by 2021-22 and all schemes including PDS across all districts of India by 2024.

 

• The initiative aligns with India's efforts to combat anaemia and malnutrition under the POSHAN Abhiyaan.

 

NOTE

 

• 2023 (Option 1), 2026 (Option 2) and 2025 (Option 3) are incorrect; the Prime Minister's announced target year for universal rice fortification coverage was 2024.

question: From which country were the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution borrowed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ireland.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution, were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland. (नीति निदेशक तत्व — आयरलैंड)

 

• Ireland itself had borrowed the concept from the Spanish Constitution. The DPSPs are non-justiciable guidelines directing the State to establish social and economic democracy.

 

• The idea was included in the Indian Constitution to balance the justiciable Fundamental Rights (Part III) with socio-economic goals the state should strive to achieve.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 37 states that DPSPs are not enforceable by any court, but are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country.

 

• Other features India borrowed from Ireland include the method of election of the President and the concept of nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha.

 

NOTE

 

• The USSR (Option 1): India borrowed the concept of Fundamental Duties from the erstwhile USSR, not DPSPs.

 

• The US (Option 2): India borrowed features such as Fundamental Rights, an independent judiciary and judicial review from the US Constitution.

 

• China (Option 4): India's Constitution does not draw any of its principal features from the Constitution of China.

question: The national poverty line for 2011-12 was estimated at _________ per capita per month for rural areas of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is ₹816.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Tendulkar Committee methodology, the national poverty line for 2011-12 was estimated at ₹816 per capita per month for rural areas and ₹1,000 per capita per month for urban areas. (गरीबी रेखा 2011-12 — ग्रामीण ₹816)

 

• The Tendulkar Committee, headed by Suresh Tendulkar, was constituted by the Planning Commission and shifted the poverty estimation methodology from a calorie-based norm to one based on spending on health, education, and nutrition.

 

• Based on this poverty line, the Planning Commission (2013) estimated that 21.9% of India's population was living below the poverty line in 2011-12.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rangarajan Committee, constituted later to review the Tendulkar methodology, estimated the 2011-12 poverty line at ₹972 per capita per month for rural areas and ₹1,407 for urban areas.

 

• Poverty estimation in India has evolved through several committees: Lakdawala (1993), Tendulkar (2009) and Rangarajan (2014).

 

NOTE

 

• ₹1,206 (Option 1), ₹760 (Option 2) and ₹900 (Option 4) do not correspond to the Tendulkar Committee's 2011-12 rural poverty line figure of ₹816.

question: The ten-day festival of Bastar Dussehra is associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bastar Dussehra is a famous 75-day-long (traditionally described as a ten-day core festival) tribal festival celebrated in the Bastar district of Chhattisgarh. (बस्तर दशहरा — छत्तीसगढ़)

 

• Unlike the Ramlila-based Dussehra celebrated elsewhere in India, Bastar Dussehra worships the local deity Goddess Danteshwari and does not involve the burning of Ravana's effigy.

 

• The festival is centred at Jagdalpur, the headquarters of Bastar district, and is marked by processions of a massive wooden chariot (Rath Parikrama) pulled by tribal communities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Goddess Danteshwari is considered the presiding deity (kuldevi) of the erstwhile Bastar royal family and is worshipped as a form of Shakti.

 

• Chhattisgarh is also known for other tribal festivals like the Madai festival.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 2), Jharkhand (Option 3) and Bihar (Option 4): Bastar Dussehra is a distinct regional tradition specific to the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh and is not associated with these states.

question: Which group of Kingdom Animalia has unsegmented, bilaterally symmetrical, soft bodies, with a triploblastic construction (comprising three layers of cells) and a lacking coelom, skeleton and anus?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Platyhelminthes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Platyhelminthes (flatworms) are triploblastic (three germ layers), bilaterally symmetrical, unsegmented, soft-bodied and acoelomate (lacking a true body cavity/coelom), and they lack a skeleton and a separate anus (they have a single opening that serves as both mouth and anus). (चपटे कृमि — प्लेटीहेल्मिन्थीज)

 

• Common examples include Planaria (free-living), Fasciola (liver fluke) and Taenia (tapeworm), many of which are parasitic.

 

• Their flattened, ribbon-like or leaf-like body shape gives the phylum its name (Greek: *platy* = flat, *helminth* = worm).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Phylum Platyhelminthes falls between the diploblastic phyla (Porifera, Cnidaria, Ctenophora) and the triploblastic coelomate/pseudocoelomate phyla in the classification of Kingdom Animalia.

 

• The excretory system in flatworms is carried out by specialised cells called flame cells.

 

NOTE

 

• Cnidaria (Option 1): Diploblastic (two germ layers), radially symmetrical animals like jellyfish and Hydra, possessing a coelenteron; they are not triploblastic.

 

• Ctenophora (Option 2): Diploblastic, radially symmetrical marine animals (comb jellies), not bilaterally symmetrical or triploblastic.

 

• Porifera (Option 4): The sponges — asymmetrical or radially symmetrical, cellular-grade organisation without true tissues, and they are not triploblastic.

question: How many classes of Indian society are mentioned in Megasthenes's book Indica?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus I Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya, wrote the book Indica, describing Mauryan society, administration and economy. (इंडिका — 7 वर्ग)

 

• In the Indica, Megasthenes divided Indian society into seven classes: Philosophers, Farmers (Cultivators), Soldiers, Herdsmen, Artisans/Traders, Magistrates (Overseers) and Councillors (Advisors to the King).

 

• Though the original text of Indica is lost, its contents survive through references in later Greek and Roman works by authors such as Strabo, Arrian and Diodorus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Megasthenes resided at the Mauryan capital Pataliputra and provided valuable, though sometimes exaggerated, eyewitness accounts of Mauryan India.

 

• Other Greek/foreign accounts of ancient India include those of Fa-Hien (Chinese, Gupta period) and Hiuen Tsang (Chinese, Harsha period).

 

NOTE

 

• 12 (Option 1), 10 (Option 2) and 5 (Option 3): These numbers do not correspond to the classification given by Megasthenes, who specifically described seven classes of Indian society.

question: Lanthenides are often called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is rare earth elements.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lanthanides (elements with atomic numbers 57 to 71, from Lanthanum to Lutetium) are collectively known as the rare earth elements, along with Scandium (21) and Yttrium (39). (लैंथेनाइड — दुर्लभ मृदा तत्व)

 

• They belong to the f-block of the periodic table (inner transition elements) and are placed separately at the bottom of the periodic table for convenience.

 

• Despite being called "rare," most lanthanides are not particularly scarce in the Earth's crust; the name reflects the difficulty historically faced in isolating and separating them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lanthanides are widely used in magnets, catalysts, phosphors, and electronics (e.g., Neodymium in permanent magnets).

 

• The Actinides (atomic numbers 89-103) form the other f-block series and include elements like Uranium and Plutonium.

 

NOTE

 

• Alkali metals (Option 1): Group 1 elements (Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr) of the s-block, distinct from lanthanides.

 

• Inert gases (Option 3): Group 18 noble gases (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn), chemically unreactive, unrelated to lanthanides.

 

• d-block elements (Option 4): The transition metals (Groups 3-12), while lanthanides belong to the f-block, not the d-block.

question: Which of the following hills is a part of the Western Ghats?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anaimalai Hills.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Anaimalai Hills (meaning "Elephant Hills"), located at the tri-junction of Kerala and Tamil Nadu, are a range within the Western Ghats. (अनाइमलाई पहाड़ियाँ — पश्चिमी घाट)

 

• They house Anamudi, the highest peak in India south of the Himalayas (2,695 m), located within the Anaimalai range.

 

• Other important hill ranges of the Western Ghats include the Nilgiri Hills, Cardamom Hills (Idukki), Palni Hills and the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Western Ghats, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is one of the world's eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity.

 

• The Palakkad Gap separates the Nilgiri Hills from the Anaimalai Hills.

 

NOTE

 

• Khasi Hills (Option 2), Jaintia Hills (Option 3) and Garo Hills (Option 4): These together form the Garo-Khasi-Jaintia hill ranges of Meghalaya, part of the Purvanchal (Eastern Hill) ranges, not the Western Ghats.

question: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Awards-2022, which was presented by President of India Droupadi Murmu on 30th November 2022, was given to _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sharath Kamal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Achanta Sharath Kamal, India's leading table tennis player, received the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2022 from President Droupadi Murmu at a ceremony held on 30 November 2022. (शरत कमल — खेल रत्न 2022)

 

• He is a multiple-time Commonwealth Games gold medallist in table tennis and became the first table tennis player to win the Khel Ratna (renamed from Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in 2021 in honour of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand).

 

• The Khel Ratna is India's highest sporting honour, awarded for the most spectacular and outstanding performance in the field of sports over a four-year period.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other National Sports Awards-2022 recipients included Nikhat Zareen (boxing), Elavenil Valarivan (shooting) and Divya Kakran (wrestling) for the Arjuna Award.

 

• The award was renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in August 2021 to honour the legendary hockey player often called the "Wizard of Hockey."

 

NOTE

 

• Venkatesh Prasad (Option 1): A former Indian cricketer (fast bowler), not a 2022 Khel Ratna recipient.

 

• Deepika Kumari (Option 3): An Indian archer; she is an Arjuna and Padma Shri awardee but did not receive the 2022 Khel Ratna.

 

• Manpreet Singh (Option 4): Former Indian men's hockey team captain; he received the Khel Ratna in 2021, not 2022.

question: The 'Pattanulkars' migrated from the Gujarat region to the Vijayanagar state. They were _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is silk weavers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pattanulkars (also called Pattunoolkarars) were a community of silk weavers who migrated from the Gujarat region to settle in the Vijayanagar Empire, primarily in present-day Tamil Nadu. (पट्टानुलकर — रेशम बुनकर)

 

• They were renowned for their expertise in silk weaving and significantly contributed to the flourishing textile trade of the Vijayanagar Empire, which was a major centre of cloth and textile production and trade.

 

• The Vijayanagar economy was substantially supported by such craft and artisan guilds, alongside flourishing agriculture and overseas trade in spices, textiles and precious stones.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vijayanagar Empire (1336-1646 CE) was founded by Harihara and Bukka and reached its zenith under Krishnadevaraya.

 

• Vijayanagar's capital, Hampi, was a major centre of trade in cotton and silk cloth, spices and precious stones, as recorded by foreign travellers like Domingo Paes and Abdur Razzaq.

 

NOTE

 

• Goldsmiths (Option 1): Not the occupation associated with the Pattanulkars community.

 

• Cotton traders (Option 2): The Pattanulkars specialised in silk, not cotton trading.

 

• Diamond makers (Option 4): Not the historically recorded occupation of the Pattanulkars community.

question: With which of the following Government of India Acts did the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms introduce Dyarchy in the provinces?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government of India Act, 1919.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of India Act, 1919, based on the recommendations of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Montford Reforms), introduced the system of Dyarchy (dual government) in the provinces. (मोंटेग्यू-चेम्सफोर्ड सुधार — द्वैध शासन 1919)

 

• Under Dyarchy, provincial subjects were divided into "Reserved" subjects (administered by the Governor with his Executive Council, e.g. law and order, finance) and "Transferred" subjects (administered by ministers responsible to the legislature, e.g. education, health, local government).

 

• The Act also introduced direct elections for the first time and expanded the legislative councils, though the franchise remained limited.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dyarchy in the provinces was later abolished by the Government of India Act, 1935, which introduced provincial autonomy and proposed Dyarchy at the centre instead.

 

• The 1919 Act also established the Central Public Service Commission and separated central and provincial budgets.

 

NOTE

 

• Government of India Act, 1945 (Option 1): No such major constitutional Act exists under this name; a distractor.

 

• Government of India Act, 1935 (Option 2): Introduced provincial autonomy (abolishing provincial Dyarchy) and proposed an All-India Federation with Dyarchy at the Centre.

 

• Government of India Act, 1923 (Option 3): No such Act exists; a distractor.

question: Who among the following was the first non-European to win a Noble prize in 1913 in literature for his work 'Gitanjali'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabindranath Tagore became the first non-European (and first Asian) to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, awarded in 1913 for his collection of poems 'Gitanjali' (Song Offerings). (रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर — नोबेल पुरस्कार 1913)

 

• He himself translated Gitanjali into English, and it was published with an introduction by the Irish poet W. B. Yeats.

 

• Tagore also composed the national anthems of India ("Jana Gana Mana") and Bangladesh ("Amar Shonar Bangla"), and founded Visva-Bharati University at Santiniketan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rabindranath Tagore renounced his British knighthood in 1919 in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

 

• India's other Nobel laureates in Literature-adjacent or related fields of note include C.V. Raman (Physics, 1930) and Amartya Sen (Economics, 1998).

 

NOTE

 

• Dwarka Nath Tagore (Option 2): Rabindranath Tagore's grandfather, a prominent entrepreneur and reformer, not a Nobel laureate.

 

• Bankim Chandra Chatterjee (Option 3): Renowned Bengali novelist and composer of "Vande Mataram," but not a Nobel Prize winner.

 

• Abanindranath Tagore (Option 4): Rabindranath's nephew, founder of the Bengal School of Art, not a Nobel laureate.

question: Ramkrishna Talukdar received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018 for his contribution to the Sattriya dance form. To which state does this dance form belong?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sattriya dance form originated in the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras) of Assam, founded by the 15th-16th century saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardeva. (सत्रिया नृत्य — असम)

 

• Ramkrishna Talukdar, a noted exponent of Sattriya, was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018 for his contribution to this dance form.

 

• Sattriya was officially recognised as one of the eight classical dance forms of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in the year 2000, the most recent addition to that list.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, is headquartered in New Delhi and gives its annual awards, known as Akademi Puraskar.

 

• Other classical dance forms of India and their states include Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha) and Manipuri (Manipur).

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal (Option 1): Known for folk forms like Chhau (also associated with Odisha/Jharkhand), not Sattriya.

 

• Meghalaya (Option 3): Known for tribal folk dances, not Sattriya.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 4): Known for the Chhau dance and tribal folk traditions, not Sattriya.

question: According to the World Meteorological Organization report reviewed during 2010-2012, the highest registered shade temperature of _________ was recorded at Al Aziziyah, Libya.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 58°C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A shade temperature of 58°C (136.4°F), recorded at Al Aziziyah, Libya on 13 September 1922, was long recognised as the highest recorded shade air temperature on Earth. (अल अजीज़िया, लीबिया — 58°C)

 

• The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) convened an international panel to review this record, and following an investigation completed in 2012, the panel found the reading to be erroneous and officially decertified it.

 

• After decertification, the highest verified temperature record was attributed to 56.7°C, recorded at Furnace Creek Ranch, Death Valley, USA, on 10 July 1913.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The WMO maintains the World Weather/Climate Extremes Archive, which records global extremes for temperature, rainfall, and other weather parameters.

 

• Death Valley, California, continues to be one of the hottest places on Earth, frequently recording temperatures above 50°C in summer.

 

NOTE

 

• 68°C (Option 2), 50°C (Option 3) and 72°C (Option 4): These figures do not match the historically recorded shade temperature of 58°C at Al Aziziyah, Libya.

question: Select the Indian musician who is associated with percussion instruments (played by striking).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Ayodhya Prasad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Ayodhya Prasad was a renowned Indian classical musician associated with the pakhawaj, a barrel-shaped percussion instrument played by striking with the hands on both ends. (अयोध्या प्रसाद — पखावज वादक)

 

• The pakhawaj is one of the oldest percussion instruments of India and is traditionally used to accompany Dhrupad vocal music and Kathak dance.

 

• Percussion (membranophone) instruments such as the pakhawaj, tabla and mridangam are all played by striking a stretched membrane, distinguishing them from stringed (chordophone) and wind (aerophone) instruments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known pakhawaj players include Gopal Das, Totaram Sharma and Bhavani Shankar.

 

• The tabla, a more widely known percussion pair-drum, evolved later and is believed to have developed from the pakhawaj.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Ravi Shankar (Option 1): A legendary sitar player, sitar being a plucked string (chordophone) instrument, not percussion.

 

• Vishwa Mohan Bhat (Option 2): Known for the Mohan Veena, a stringed (chordophone) instrument he innovated, not percussion.

 

• Bismillah Khan (Option 4): A maestro of the shehnai, a wind (aerophone) instrument, not a percussion instrument.

question: Rovers Cup is associated with which game?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Football.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rovers Cup is one of the oldest football tournaments in India, first held in 1891 in Mumbai (Bombay). (रोवर्स कप — फुटबॉल)

 

• It was founded by the Bombay Gymkhana and is among the oldest football tournaments in Asia, historically dominated by teams from the armed forces and Mumbai-based clubs.

 

• The tournament played a significant role in popularising football in India during the colonial era.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other historic Indian football tournaments include the Durand Cup (Asia's oldest football tournament, since 1888), the IFA Shield, and the Santosh Trophy.

 

• The Durand Cup is held in New Delhi/Kolkata and is organised by the Durand Football Tournament Society.

 

NOTE

 

• Tennis (Option 1): Associated with tournaments like the Davis Cup and Wimbledon, not the Rovers Cup.

 

• Badminton (Option 2): Associated with tournaments like the Thomas Cup and Uber Cup, not the Rovers Cup.

 

• Hockey (Option 4): Associated with tournaments like the Beighton Cup and the Agha Khan Cup, not the Rovers Cup.

question: Article 323 of the Indian Constitution deals with _________.
option_4: power to extend functions of Public Services Commissions
solution_text:
The correct answer is reports of Public Services Commissions.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 323 of the Indian Constitution, under Part XIV, deals with the reports of the Union and State Public Service Commissions. (अनुच्छेद 323 — लोक सेवा आयोग की रिपोर्ट)

 

• It mandates that the UPSC shall present its annual report on its work to the President, who lays it before both Houses of Parliament, while a State Public Service Commission presents its report to the Governor, who lays it before the State Legislature.

 

• Along with the report, a memorandum explaining the cases where the Commission's advice was not accepted, and the reasons for such rejection, is also to be laid before the legislature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Provisions relating to Public Service Commissions are covered under Articles 315 to 323 in Part XIV of the Constitution.

 

• Article 320 deals with the functions of Public Service Commissions, while Article 322 deals with their expenses.

 

NOTE

 

• Expenses of Public Services Commissions (Option 1): This is covered under Article 322, not Article 323.

 

• Functions of Public Services Commissions (Option 3): This is covered under Article 320, not Article 323.

 

• Power to extend functions of Public Services Commissions (Option 4): This is covered under Article 321, not Article 323.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding cell membrane?

I. The membrane is selectively permeable to some molecules present on either side of it.

II. Water may also move across this membrane from lower to higher concentration.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: The cell (plasma) membrane is selectively permeable, allowing only certain molecules to pass across it while restricting others, thus regulating the movement of substances into and out of the cell. (कोशिका झिल्ली — चयनात्मक पारगम्यता)

 

• Statement II is incorrect: In osmosis, water moves across a selectively permeable membrane from a region of higher water concentration (lower solute concentration) to a region of lower water concentration (higher solute concentration) — i.e., from higher to lower concentration of water, not from lower to higher as stated.

 

• This directional movement of water continues until the solute concentrations on both sides of the membrane become equal (equilibrium), or until it is opposed by an equal and opposite hydrostatic pressure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Osmosis is a special case of diffusion involving only the solvent (water) across a selectively/semi-permeable membrane.

 

• The plasma membrane follows the Fluid Mosaic Model, proposed by Singer and Nicolson (1972), consisting of a phospholipid bilayer embedded with proteins.

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 1): Incorrect, since Statement I is also a true fact about the cell membrane.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 3): Incorrect, since Statement I is factually correct.

 

• Both I and II (Option 4): Incorrect, since Statement II wrongly describes the direction of water movement across the membrane.

question: How many substitute players are there in a Beach Volleyball team?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Beach Volleyball, each team consists of only two players on court, and no substitutions are allowed during a match. (बीच वॉलीबॉल — कोई स्थानापन्न नहीं)

 

• This is a key difference from indoor volleyball, where a team has 6 players on court with up to 6 substitute players permitted.

 

• Since there are no substitutes, both players on a beach volleyball team must play the entire match without a break, covering the whole 8m x 8m half-court alone.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Beach Volleyball became an official Olympic sport at the 1996 Atlanta Games.

 

• A standard beach volleyball court measures 16m x 8m, smaller than an indoor volleyball court (18m x 9m).

 

NOTE

 

• 3 (Option 1), 2 (Option 3) and 1 (Option 4): Incorrect, as beach volleyball rules do not allow any substitute players during a match.

question: Identify the INCORRECT statement in the context of Microfinance Institutions in India.
option_1: A microfinance loan is given to a household having annual household income up to ₹3,00,000.
option_2: A microfinance loan is a collateral-free loan.
option_3: When giving a micro loan, a household means an individual family unit, i.e., husband, wife, and their unmarried children.
option_4: A microfinance loan should be linked with a lien on the deposit account of the borrower.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A microfinance loan should be linked with a lien on the deposit account of the borrower.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the RBI Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Regulatory Framework for Microfinance Loans) Directions, 2022, a microfinance loan explicitly shall NOT be linked with a lien on the deposit account of the borrower, making this statement incorrect. (माइक्रोफाइनेंस ऋण — जमा खाते पर बंधक नहीं)

 

• The Directions define a "microfinance loan" as a collateral-free loan given to a household with annual household income up to ₹3,00,000, regardless of whether the household is rural or urban.

 

• A "household" is defined as an individual family unit, i.e., husband, wife and their unmarried children, whether or not they are living together.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• These Directions, effective from 1 April 2022, removed the earlier interest-rate cap on microfinance loans, instead requiring boards of Regulated Entities (REs) to adopt a policy ensuring interest rates are not usurious.

 

• The framework applies uniformly across all Regulated Entities (REs) — Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks, NBFC-MFIs and NBFCs.

 

NOTE

 

• Household income up to ₹3,00,000 (Option 1): This is a correct statement, matching the RBI's definition of a qualifying microfinance loan.

 

• Collateral-free loan (Option 2): This is a correct statement; RBI mandates that microfinance loans must be collateral-free.

 

• Household definition (Option 3): This is a correct statement, matching the RBI's definition of "household" for microfinance purposes.

question: The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change notified the E-Waste Management Rules in 2022. These rules are supposed to be come into force from _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 April 2023.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) notified the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, which came into force from 1 April 2023. (ई-कचरा प्रबंधन नियम 2022 — 1 अप्रैल 2023 से लागू)

 

• These rules replaced the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2016, and introduced an Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regime with a online trading system for EPR certificates.

 

• The rules mandate producers, manufacturers, and recyclers to register on a centralised online portal developed by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) for monitoring compliance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 apply to 106 items of Electrical and Electronic Equipment (EEE), including new categories like solar photovoltaic panels/cells/modules.

 

• India is one of the world's largest generators of e-waste, and these rules aim to promote a circular economy in electronic waste management.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 July 2023 (Option 2), 1 December 2022 (Option 3) and 1 January 2023 (Option 4): Incorrect; the rules were officially notified to come into force from 1 April 2023.
